I reproduced CR-3 with real public APIs and no injected state or source patch: 3 of 3 runs hit the target `AssertionError` at `AbstractDistribZkTestBase.java:185`, and a run with the fix applied passes. Upstream already reported and fixed this exact defect as SOLR-9440. The pinned tree predates that fix, so Novelty is KNOWN and the verdict stays REPRODUCED.

- **Source**: Code Review
- **Novelty**: KNOWN (cite: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SOLR-9440 ; fix-status: fixed — upstream fix 39376cd (master) / f6f5d01 (branch_7x), released in 7.2 and 8.0. The pinned base 1eaa00b is 7.2-dev and its CHANGES.txt has no SOLR-9440 entry, so the fix is not in this tree)
- **Location**: solr/solrj/src/java/org/apache/solr/common/cloud/ZkStateReader.java:1342

## Description
When the last watcher on a collection is removed, `ZkStateReader.removeCollectionStateWatcher` (`ZkStateReader.java:1342-1351`) deletes only the `collectionWatches` entry. It leaves the cached `watchedCollectionStates[coll]` in place, adds no `LazyCollectionRef`, and does not rebuild the cluster state. `unregisterCore` (`:1252-1268`) does all three.

Three things keep that stale cache in place:
- `constructState` (`:547-554`) prefers the watched entry over the lazy one.
- `StateWatcher.process` (`:1033-1036`) ignores ZooKeeper events once the collection is no longer watched.
- The eviction in `updateWatchedCollection` (`:1402-1405`) never runs on this path.

So a reader with no local cores, such as a `CloudSolrClient`'s reader, freezes its view of the collection at the moment the last watcher was removed.

## Trigger scenario
This is a variant of the workload `TestCloudRecovery`, in the same module, `solr/core`:
1. Set up as in `TestCloudRecovery.setupCluster`: 2 nodes, `collection1` with 2 shards × 2 NRT replicas. `waitForRecoveriesToFinish(30)` passes here because the collection is still lazy in the client reader.
2. `ChaosMonkey.stop(jetty0)`. The node's shutdown publishes its replicas DOWN (`CoreContainer.java:749`).
3. `cluster.getSolrClient().waitForState(COLLECTION, 60s, <the stopped node's replicas are DOWN>)`. This registers a watcher and removes it again (`ZkStateReader.java:1311-1331` → `:1342`). The view is now frozen at znodeVersion 7 or 9, with two replicas DOWN.
4. `ChaosMonkey.start(jetty0)`. The node comes back on the same port and name, and its replicas recover to ACTIVE in ZooKeeper.
5. `AbstractDistribZkTestBase.waitForRecoveriesToFinish(COLLECTION, cluster.getSolrClient().getZkStateReader(), false, true, 30)`. Live nodes are refreshed on their own (`:737-738`), so a frozen DOWN replica on a live node makes `sawLiveRecovering` true on every one of the 31 polls. The call then fails at `:185`.

The modeling brief assumed the poller reads `state.json` fresh (`:689-693`). That holds only while the collection is lazy in the client reader. It is true for the unmodified workload and false after any `waitForState` on that reader.

## Developer intent
- The local git history is a single squashed commit, so blame shows nothing.
- The comment at `:1402` ("Resolve race with unregisterCore") shows that evicting caches for unwatched collections is intended behaviour.
- In SOLR-9440, Shalin Shekhar Mangar identifies this exact site: "The bug is in ZkStateReader.removeCollectionStateWatcher which only removes the collection from … collectionWatches map … So a cached DocCollection reference that is neither lazy nor watched is left behind." The issue description adds: "any call to waitForRecoveriesToFinish would see stale state and loop until timeout."
- The novelty search ran only after the reproduction verdict was settled, as Shared Rule 2 of the ad hoc skill requires, and it set only the Novelty field. All queries are recorded in `confirmation/CR-3/investigation.md`.
- The bug-confirmation pre-filter would have dropped a code-review finding that is already known (DROPPED). The adhoc-coordination section takes precedence and says the search must not change the verdict, so CR-3 stays REPRODUCED with Novelty KNOWN.

## Reproduction result
**Level 0** (black-box). Command: `repro/test_bugCR-3_frozen_view_after_watcher_removal.sh`, which runs `ant … test -Dtestcase=SpeculaCR3FrozenViewTest -Dtests.method=frozenViewAfterLastWatcherRemoved -Dtests.jvms=1 -Dtests.useSecurityManager=false`. The test source is `repro/SpeculaCR3FrozenViewTest.java`, built in the CR-3 worktree at the base commit. `ZkStateReader.java` there is identical to base; the tracing added by the trace-validation harness is inert unless `-Dspecula.trace.file` is set.

- **Bug lines:** "stale view … znodeVersion=7 … down" while "ZK truth … znodeVersion=13 … all active", followed by "TARGET FIRED" with the frame `AbstractDistribZkTestBase.waitForRecoveriesToFinish(AbstractDistribZkTestBase.java:185)`. That is the target's exception type, file and line.
- **Expected behaviour:** a fresh reader, which loads the collection lazily, reports recoveries finished. That is the CONTROL line.
- **Fix control:** `repro/test_bugCR-3_fix_control.patch` makes `removeCollectionStateWatcher` mirror `unregisterCore`. With it, the run prints `stale view: lazy=true znodeVersion=12 [... all active]` and `RESULT NOT_REPRODUCED: waitForRecoveriesToFinish passed after 0s` (`repro/CR-3_fixcontrol.log`). The patch was reverted afterwards, and run 3 on the unpatched build reproduced again.

Checklist:
1. **Level 0 or 1 alone? Yes.** Level 0 only: public APIs (`MiniSolrCloudCluster`, `ChaosMonkey.stop`/`start`, `CloudSolrClient.waitForState`, `waitForRecoveriesToFinish`), with no timing hooks, state injection or source patch.
2. Not applicable, since no Level 2 or 3 was used. The test never writes the guard's operands or touches the target method.
3. **Real consumer:** `AbstractDistribZkTestBase.waitForRecoveriesToFinish` (`AbstractDistribZkTestBase.java:185`) throws `AssertionError` even though ZooKeeper shows every replica active. Any other caller of `getClusterState()` on that `CloudSolrClient` reader, such as `ClusterStateUtil.waitForAllActiveAndLiveReplicas`, reads the same frozen view.
4. **Permanent?** Yes, until someone registers a new watcher or core, or calls `forceUpdate`. Over 30+ seconds, the ZooKeeper updates from version 7 to 13 never reached the reader. The only thing that cleared it was the test's own re-registration in step 7, which happened after the failure. Nothing in the poller or in `ZkStateReader`'s event handling resolves it, so it is not masked.

Persistent record: `confirmation/CR-3/issue.json`. It passed the findings validator (`valid: true`). I left its `invariants` field empty because naming `TargetSafe` there requires model files I'm not allowed to open; `TargetSafe` is named in the consequence text instead.

## Recommendation
Port SOLR-9440 (commit 39376cd). In `removeCollectionStateWatcher`, when `canBeRemoved()` is true, do what `unregisterCore` does: `watchedCollectionStates.remove(collection)`, `lazyCollectionStates.put(collection, new LazyCollectionRef(collection))`, then call `constructState(Collections.emptySet())` under `getUpdateLock()`. This is exactly the patch the fix-control run used. Until the fix is in, tests that call `waitForState` on the client reader before `waitForRecoveriesToFinish` can work around it with `registerCore(collection)` (the workaround in SOLR-9440) or `forceUpdateCollection` before polling.

Sources: [SOLR-9440](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SOLR-9440), [dev@lucene thread](https://go.mail-archive.com/dev@lucene.apache.org/msg242870.html)
